questions.q: What are the FinOps dashboard's four panels?
options: Daily spend by cloud, cost per namespace, cluster-wide CPU/memory utilization, and budget burn-down
Latency per service, error rate, request volume, and uptime
Pod count, node count, deployment count, and namespace count
Only one panel: total monthly spend
questions.explain: The dashboard covers daily spend by cloud, cost attributed per namespace, cluster-wide utilization, and budget burn-down against the sale-period budget.

questions.q: What specific question does the cluster-wide average CPU/memory utilization panel answer?
options: Which individual pod is slowest right now
Across all the compute Driftwood is paying for in apppool, how much of it is being used in total
Which availability zone has the most pods
How many customers are currently checking out
questions.explain: A cluster-wide average answers a total-utilization question — it's the standard, defensible figure for judging whether the node pool's autoscaler range is sized correctly for the money being spent.

questions.q: Is building the FinOps dashboard around a cluster-wide average considered a mistake in this lesson?
options: Yes, it should have used per-zone averages from the start
No — it's a reasonable, standard design choice for the specific cost/capacity question a FinOps dashboard exists to answer
Yes, averages are never appropriate for dashboards
No, because the dashboard doesn't use averages at all
questions.explain: The lesson is explicit that nothing about building it this way is a mistake — a cluster-wide average is the defensible choice for answering 'how much total capacity is used.'

questions.q: What can a cluster-wide average NOT tell you, by construction?
options: The total compute being paid for
How evenly utilization is distributed — twelve nodes at 20% and three nodes pinned at 95% can average out to something healthy-looking
The daily spend in dollars
Which cloud provider is being used
questions.explain: An average answers 'how much, in total,' not 'how evenly distributed' — an uneven cluster can still produce a comfortable, unremarkable average.

questions.q: What kind of question does the lesson say belongs on a DIFFERENT dashboard than this FinOps one?
options: Total daily spend
Whether any single part of the cluster is struggling right now — a reliability question (latency, error rates per service), not a cost or capacity one
Cost per namespace
Budget burn-down versus forecast
questions.explain: The lesson draws a deliberate seam: this dashboard answers 'are we spending what we expected on the capacity we have,' while 'is anything actually struggling right now' is a reliability question for a separate dashboard.
